No mathematical repair is needed.The decisive structural step is valid: the exact cut slack contains  $|E(U,W)|$ , so regular equality forces the witnesses to supply all their remaining degrees within  $W$ . The subsequent colour balance and simplicity obstruction follow.1. Equality forces the claimed ledger templateSince  $k\ge4$ , every coefficient in the displayed equality certificate is strictly positive; in particular,  $2k-7\ge1$ . The prior inequalities give
$$J,D,F\ge0,\qquad T-2d,\ R-2d,\ B-2d\ge0,$$
and all the remaining counts are nonnegative. Consequently, equality forces
$$J=D=F=0,\qquad T=R=B=2d,
\qquad s=\mu=b_3=z_0=0.$$
The remaining algebra is exact. From  $D=0$ ,
$$q=2b_2.$$
From  $R=T=2d$ ,
$$c=2d+b_2,\qquad a=2d-b_2.$$
Therefore
$$0=J=c+2q-a-2b_2
=(2d+b_2)+4b_2-(2d-b_2)-2b_2
=4b_2.$$
Thus
$$\boxed{q=b_2=0,\qquad c=a=t=2d,\qquad e=4d.}$$
Every selected star has at least two leaves, and  $e=2c$ . Hence every selected star has exactly two leaves and is  $P_3$ .For the remaining vertex counts, the whole-cut note’s equations (6) and (7) reduce to
$$n=12d+m+u,\qquad B=4d+m-u=2d.$$
Thus  $u=m+2d$ , and
$$(12k-14)d=n=14d+2m.$$
It follows that
$$\boxed{m=(6k-14)d,\qquad u=(6k-12)d.}$$
There is no factor-of-two error:  $m$  counts vertices in selected edge components, so the number of those components is  $(3k-7)d$ .Also,  $n=(12k-14)d>0$  implies  $d>0$ , and integrality gives  $d\ge1$ .2. Exactly one private witness and one distinct-helper witness occur at each centreThere are exactly two chosen leaf witnesses per centre, and  $q=0$  means there are no additional direct deletion witnesses. The accepted assignment chooses at least one private witness at every centre.Since  $b_2=b_3=z_0=0$ , every selected isolate has  $h(i)=1$ . Therefore
$$H=\sum_{i\in I}h(i)=a=c.$$
Each chosen witness has at most one isolate helper. Hence  $H=c$  counts exactly  $c$  helped witnesses. On the other hand, each centre has two witnesses, at least one of which is private, so each centre contributes at most one helped witness. There are  $c$  centres and exactly  $c$  helped witnesses. Therefore every centre contributes exactly one.This proves that each centre has:exactly one private leaf witness;exactly one helped leaf witness;exactly one isolate helper for that helped witness.The helpers are distinct because a helper used by two chosen witnesses would have  $h(i)\ge2$ , contrary to  $b_2=b_3=0$ . The argument uses the stipulated single fixed witness assignment throughout.3. The actual cut-slack identity is correctWrite
$$\deg(X):=\sum_{v\in X}\deg_G(v).$$
The accepted neighbourhood classification gives the exact identity
$$|E(S,U)|=\deg(S)-3e-m-q-H.$$
Using
$$\epsilon_S=k|S|-\deg(S),\qquad
\epsilon_U=ku-\deg(U),$$
together with  $|S|=3c+s+t+m+z_0$ , direct expansion yields
$$\begin{aligned}
\widehat F
&=F_k+\epsilon_S-\epsilon_U\\
&=7c+4s+3q+m+\deg(U)-\deg(S).
\end{aligned}$$
Since  $e=2c+s$ , the exact expression for  $|E(S,U)|$  then gives
$$\widehat F
=(c+s+2q-H)+\deg(U)-|E(S,U)|.$$
Because  $S,W,U$  partition the vertex set,
$$\deg(U)
=|E(S,U)|+2|E(G[U])|+|E(U,W)|.$$
Consequently,
$$\boxed{\widehat F
=(c+s+2q-H)+2|E(G[U])|+|E(U,W)|.}$$
Both multiplicities are correct: an edge internal to  $U$  contributes two to  $\deg(U)$ , while an edge from  $U$  to  $W$  contributes one.At regular equality,
$$\epsilon_S=\epsilon_U=0,\quad F=0,\quad s=q=0,\quad H=c.$$
Thus
$$0=2|E(G[U])|+|E(U,W)|,$$
which forces
$$\boxed{E(G[U])=\varnothing,\qquad E(U,W)=\varnothing.}$$
A private witness has exactly one selected neighbour, and a helped witness has exactly two. Neither has a neighbour in  $U$ . Regularity therefore gives internal degrees in  $G[W]$  of exactly  $k-1$  and  $k-2$ , respectively.4. Colour balance forces  $c_A=c_B=d$ The colour placement is correct. A selected leaf has the opposite colour to its centre. Its outside witness is adjacent to that leaf, so the witness has the same colour as the centre. A helper adjacent to that witness has the opposite colour.Thus, if  $c_A,c_B$  count the centres in the two fixed bipartition classes, then  $W_A$  contains  $c_A$  private and  $c_A$  helped witnesses, while  $W_B$  contains  $c_B$  of each type.Counting the edges of the bipartite graph  $G[W]$  from its two sides gives
$$(k-1)c_A+(k-2)c_A
=(k-1)c_B+(k-2)c_B,$$
or
$$(2k-3)c_A=(2k-3)c_B.$$
Since  $2k-3>0$  and  $c_A+c_B=c=2d$ ,
$$\boxed{c_A=c_B=d.}$$
Each witness part therefore has  $2d$  vertices, with exactly  $d$  of internal degree  $k-1$  and  $d$  of internal degree  $k-2$ .Because  $d>0$ , there is a private witness. Its  $k-1$  neighbours are distinct vertices of the opposite witness part, by simplicity. Hence
$$k-1\le2d,$$
and therefore
$$\boxed{d\ge\left\lceil\frac{k-1}{2}\right\rceil
=\left\lfloor\frac{k}{2}\right\rfloor.}$$
The claimed exclusions follow:For  $k=4,n=34$ , equality would require  $d=1$ , but the necessary bound is  $d\ge2$ .For  $k=5,n=46$ , equality would again require  $d=1$ , but the necessary bound is  $d\ge2$ .These are exclusions of the stated equality instances.5. The cyclic-shift witness-interface realization works throughout the stated rangeLet  $N=2d$ , with  $d\ge\lfloor k/2\rfloor$ . Then
$$N\ge k-1,\qquad k-2\le N-1.$$
Take disjoint left and right copies of  $\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$ , and insert
$$i_L\sim(i+j)_R
\qquad (j=1,\ldots,k-2).$$
The shifts are distinct and nonzero modulo  $N$ , so there are no repeated edges and no diagonal edges in this first stage. Every left vertex has degree  $k-2$ . Every right vertex also has degree  $k-2$ , because each shift is a bijection.Now add
$$i_L\sim i_R,\qquad 0\le i<d.$$
These edges are absent from the first stage and form a matching. They increase the degree of exactly  $d$  vertices in each part by one. Consequently, each part has exactly: $d$  designated private vertices of degree  $k-1$ ; $d$  designated helped vertices of degree  $k-2$ .Equal labels on opposite sides identify different vertices, so these diagonal edges are not loops. The construction also works at the smallest admissible  $d$ .Its scope is exactly as stated: it realizes the required bipartite degree sequence on  $W$ . It does not supply the remaining vertices and incidences of a full equality graph, prove minimal formation for a completed selection, or establish that a completed graph has the required dissociation optimum.6. The no-selected-edge rectangle consequence is validUse the accepted boundary extension, equation (15), with  $k=4$  and  $m=0$ . It gives
$$\boxed{8d+c+q\le\epsilon_S-\epsilon_U.}$$
For positive integers  $h,w$ , the full rectangular grid has
$$|V|=hw,\qquad |E|=h(w-1)+w(h-1)=2hw-h-w.$$
Therefore
$$\epsilon_V=\sum_{v\in V}(4-\deg(v))
=4hw-2|E|=2h+2w.$$
Since  $S,W,U$  partition  $V$ ,
$$\epsilon_S-\epsilon_U
=\epsilon_V-\epsilon_W-2\epsilon_U
\le2h+2w,$$
because all degree deficits are nonnegative. Combining the two inequalities,
$$8d+c+q\le\epsilon_S-\epsilon_U\le2h+2w.$$
Integrality of  $d$  now gives
$$\boxed{
d\le
\left\lfloor\frac{2h+2w-c-q}{8}\right\rfloor
\le
\left\lfloor\frac{h+w}{4}\right\rfloor.
}$$
The second inequality uses only  $c,q\ge0$ .No assumption  $d>0$  enters this argument, so it remains valid for  $d=0$  and  $d<0$ , including when the first floor is negative. One-row and one-column rectangles are also covered: the edge-count formula remains valid, and the cited boundary extension has no minimum-degree requirement.This is precisely a perimeter cap for the specified selected-star minimal sets with  $m=0$ .
